claims.text: Adding temperature-dependent longitudinal spin fluctuations and short-range-order terms to CALPHAD will significantly improve melting-temperature and entropy-of-fusion predictions for magnetic and refractory HEAs.
The modified framework will outperform models based on static magnetic moments and random atomic distributions.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations thermally induce magnetic moments in Co, Cr, and Ni in CoCrFeMnNi.
The magnetic moments of Co, Cr, and Ni in CoCrFeMnNi increase with temperature.
Short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr can produce HfTi and TiZr clusters.
HfTi and TiZr pairs in HfNbTaTiZr exhibit attractive short-range-order tendencies.
Short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr can form B2-ordered structures.
The relevant short-range-order interactions can be represented by specific pair-attraction energies in the thermodynamic potential.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations and short-range-order clusters alter the free-energy landscape of the alloys.
These magnetic and chemical mediators reduce the free-energy barrier for phase transitions.
These mediators modify the vibrational entropy contribution near the melting point.
In MoNbTaW, a thermal entropy contribution increases linearly with temperature and lowers the free-energy barrier for kink-pair nucleation.
The linear thermal-entropy behavior observed for dislocation motion is applicable to the proposed melting thermodynamics.
Magnetic and short-range-order contributions collectively shift Gibbs free-energy curves and thereby correct predicted melting temperatures and entropies of fusion.
The modified method will predict melting temperatures within ±50 K of experiment for magnetic and refractory HEAs.
Standard CALPHAD models will have melting-temperature deviations greater than 100 K because magnetic and short-range-order contributions are omitted.
The modified method will predict entropy of fusion more accurately for systems with complex short-range order.
The method is valid when Co, Cr, or Ni is present and short-range-order formation has negative interaction parameters.
The method may lose accuracy for nonmagnetic refractory systems with negligible short-range order or for systems that form distinct intermetallic phases through strongly positive mixing enthalpy.
LSF parameters derived over 50–1200 K may not extrapolate reliably to melting temperatures above 2000 K without experimental validation.

contradictions.description: The outcome broadly promises accuracy for refractory HEAs and the falsification rule uses nonmagnetic HfNbTaTiZr, while the stated validity boundary requires magnetic elements together with favorable SRO and warns that nonmagnetic refractory systems may fall outside the method's accurate regime.
